facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He is working as a project manager at a logistics company.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work involves excessive hours
facts.content: Daniel stays at his desk answering messages late at night. He thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night. Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible, with most nights he sleeps about four hours. He wakes up at 3 AM and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours. I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Headaches upon waking
facts.content: When Daniel wakes at 3 AM, his head hurts. He thinks about shipping schedules, the client, or forgotten things.
facts.evidence: My head just hurts. Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights. He lies until about 5 AM before getting up to make tea.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's symptoms
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated. He is having a dream and is always being the strong one.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, he's slower, he gets frustrated. He's having a dream and he's always being the strong one.

facts.heading: Drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, and it takes about an hour each way.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Sole caregiver burden
facts.content: Daniel is the one who handles all the care for his father. His angry sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls of me.

facts.heading: Guilt about expressing needs
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying he is tired. He does not say anything to anyone, including Hannah.
facts.evidence: He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill. So I don't say anything to anyone. Not to Hanach either?

facts.heading: Sister calls father weekly
facts.content: Hannah calls their father every Sunday.
facts.evidence: She calls him every Sunday.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests which were all normal. The GP said it is stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: GP advised no talking
facts.content: The GP said Daniel had no time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: she said I hadn't got the time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked her
facts.content: A girlfriend named Claire booked time with Daniel. Claire said she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: A girlfriend booked her, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is very patient and makes Daniel tea. She does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire is worrying
facts.content: Daniel can see that Claire is worrying about herself too.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's worrying about her too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause stress
facts.content: The emails are what stop Daniel from saying yes to plans. Daniel will have to respond to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a price. He cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Ran before October
facts.content: Daniel ran before October. He went running three years every Saturday morning for six years.
facts.evidence: I ran. I'm going to be three years every Saturday morning. I've done it for six years.

facts.heading: Stopped running recently
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. His legs feel like lead now.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He felt that running was the one time nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: Peterson. He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11, at night, and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answering emails always
facts.content: Daniel answers every email, even if he is not bad. Claire hates this behavior.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm not bad. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that his boss might let him go due to a restructuring this spring.
facts.evidence: Dan hates the thing I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Relief and guilt
facts.content: Daniel thinks he might feel relieved if he is let go, but he would feel horrible about it because he has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved. I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Tiredness and irritability
facts.content: Daniel feels flat and irritable apart from tiredness.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Panic attack symptoms
facts.content: Daniel slept at a colleague and sat in the toilets for ten minutes. His heart was going and his hands were shaking.
facts.evidence: I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes. Heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Heart attack thought
facts.content: Daniel thought for a second that what he experienced was a heart attack, but it passed.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Had frightening experience
facts.content: Daniel has had frightening experiences on a train. He had not told anyone about it.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform. I hadn't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel is afraid of losing control. He fears he is losing it or coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day

facts.heading: Evening wine use
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off. He drinks two to three glasses.
facts.evidence: and I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine effect duration
facts.content: The wine helps for about an hour. Daniel wakes up at three anyway.
facts.evidence: Easy. It works for an hour. I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Wine feeling unhelpful
facts.content: Daniel feels the wine is not useful. He feels like he is listing everything wrong with him.
facts.evidence: It doesn't feel useful. Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Carrying burdens at night
facts.content: Daniel thinks he carries things during the nights. He thinks he could cope if he could sleep.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior pattern
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything. He just got on with it.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything. Not once. That's the same. Just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks he is not weak. He thinks he is just very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. Just very tired.

facts.heading: Willingness to try small steps
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try something small. He suggests a fixed time to switch off his phone.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small? Very small. A fixed time in the evening when you switch off your phone, even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Proposed time for phone off
facts.content: Daniel suggests half past nine as a time to switch off his phone.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Feeling after sharing thoughts
facts.content: Daniel felt strange but also a bit of relief after saying what he was carrying.
facts.evidence: Strange Bit of relief actually Like putting it on bad but I didn't realize I was carrying

facts.heading: Current feeling state
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter right now. He feels shaky after speaking.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again next week. He will try to be on time.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here I'll try to make it on time
